_comment: Rubric-first. Fill the five human verdicts; that is the whole job. Open a rubric's findings and label them only when you DISAGREE with its verdict, or on a periodic spot-check — verdict agreement is not reasoning agreement, so an occasional drill-down keeps a right-for-the-wrong-reason FAIL from passing unnoticed.
_verdicts_note: lint is decided by scripts, not a judge — a human FAIL there grades the RULE, not a model. groundedness and conformance are zero-tolerance (any finding = FAIL). coherence and tone are holistic: findings can exist alongside a PASS.
_overall_note: Never set a human overall. It is derived: PASS iff human lint AND groundedness AND conformance all PASS. coherence and tone are advisory and never enter the gate.

findings.summary: one-line copy of the judge's finding

_blind_note: Set to {"human_found": <n>, "judge_matched": <n>} only if you wrote your own findings BEFORE reading the judge file. Otherwise leave null — a guessed recall number is worse than none.
_note_field: verdicts.<rubric>.note is free text — use it when you DISAGREE, to say why. That sentence is what becomes a worked example in the rubric; a disagreement without one is a number nobody can act on later.
